lines.text: When I arrive, not will arrive!
Many learners say: I will call you when I will arrive.
Better: I will call you when I arrive.
After when, use the simple form.
Arrive! Call me when you arrive there.

data.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
data.right: I will call you when I arrive.
data.why: After when, use the simple form.

native.tip: En español “cuando llegue”, pero en inglés tras “when” va el presente: “when I arrive.”

en.tip: Spanish “cuando llegue” sounds like the future, but English uses the present after “when”: “when I arrive.”
